profiles.name: T-Jay Fry
profiles.description: T-Jay Fry was arrested in connection with Lancaster’s September 2020 racial-justice protest. A September 17 report confirmed that he remained in county jail after his September 14 arrest. In September 2022 he pleaded guilty to failure to disperse and defiant trespass and was ordered to pay fines and costs. His precise jail-release date and later custody status remain unverified.
profiles.finding: Lancaster police arrest list and One United Lancaster are original-source leads; portrait not yet inspected.

profiles.name: Ryan David Lucero
profiles.description: Ryan David Lucero, 33, of Magna UT, charged September 9, 2020 with influencing a federal officer by threat after threatening to murder a Department of Veterans Affairs police officer following the May 30, 2020 SLC riots. The threat was found in the officers mailbox by his teenage daughter. Pleaded guilty; 9 months / time served + $100 special assessment.
profiles.finding: KSL Magna VA-officer threat report matches identity; third-party 2019 mugshot requires original-source confirmation.

profiles.name: Tearra NaAsia Guthrie
profiles.description: Tearra NaAsia Guthrie was 23 and from Charleston when charged September 8, 2020 with civil disorder for the May 30, 2020 Charleston BLM protest. Pleaded guilty; 7 months federal prison (terrorism-enhancement-applied guideline cap of 5 years was avoided in plea). Died May 2022.
profiles.finding: Charleston public index corroboration only; no accepted portrait. Obituary follow-up remains.

profiles.name: Ronald T. Green
profiles.description: Ronald T. Green, 24, of Youngstown OH, threw an object through the rear window of a Youngstown police cruiser during the May 31, 2020 BLM protest; also charged federally as a felon in possession of ammunition (prior 2015 Texas burglary conviction). Sentenced September 3, 2020 to 10 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Hydrogeologist namesake excluded; Youngstown-specific follow-up remains.

profiles.name: Marcello Earle Woods
profiles.description: Marcello Earle Woods, 28, of Columbia SC, was charged September 1, 2020 with destroying a Columbia Police Department vehicle by fire on May 30, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 18 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Columbia police 2020 annual report PDF lead, no verified portrait yet.

profiles.name: Raphael Shaw
profiles.description: Raphael Shaw, 20, broke into a Wells Fargo on West Philadelphias 52nd Street corridor on May 31, 2020 wearing a blonde wig, pointed a rifle at people inside, and used a stolen Lowes forklift to remove a $104,000 cash vault. Pleaded guilty; time served (~12 months) + 15 months supervised release + $104,000 restitution.
profiles.finding: Inquirer Wells Fargo case report lead; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Xavier Nolley-Hall
profiles.description: Xavier Nolley-Hall, 20, was with Raphael Shaw entering the West Philadelphia Wells Fargo with intent to steal money during the May 31, 2020 BLM-related civil unrest. Charged August 25, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 45 days federal prison.
profiles.finding: Federal Pennsylvania court PDF identifies defendant; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Jesse Shackelford
profiles.description:
Jesse Shackelford is a prison abolitionist and a CUNY law student who, after the 2020 Uprisings, was called to serve upon a grand jury meant to persecute those involved with the Black liberation struggle and uprisings in Madison. Joining a long history of grand jury resisters, Shackelford claimed his Fifth Amendment right to silence. He was charged with civil contempt.

He was taken into civil-contempt custody on August 19, 2020. His precise release date has not been verified.
profiles.finding: Its Going Down support page failed direct fetch; athlete, academic and electrician namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Corey Smith
profiles.description: Corey Smith, 24, gender non-conforming, with co-defendant Elaine Carberry, set fire to a marked NYPD Homeless Outreach Unit van on University Place at 4:35 a.m. July 15, 2020. Charged August 11, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 6 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Musician, author, photographer, football and real-estate namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Elaine Carberry
profiles.description: Elaine Carberry, 36, with Corey Smith set fire to an NYPD Homeless Outreach van on July 15, 2020 in NYC. Charged August 11, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 6 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: No adequately identified portrait in initial results; NYC case-specific follow-up remains.

profiles.name: Mario Ernesto Alvarado
profiles.description: Mario Ernesto Alvarado, 42, charged August 4, 2020 with arson for setting fire to Pizzeria Mozza / Mozza2Go in Hollywood during the May 30, 2020 LA protests; $550,000 in damage. Pleaded guilty February 28, 2022; 12 months and 1 day federal prison + 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Beverly Press August 2020 PDF lead; Salvadoran driver and design-portfolio namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Shelby Ligons
profiles.description: Shelby Ligons, 22, of Nashville, charged August 3, 2020 with malicious destruction of property by fire after she set fire to a poster reading slogans against police and placed it inside a window of the Nashville Metro Courthouse on May 30, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 12 months and 1 day federal prison + 3 years supervised release + $500 restitution.
profiles.finding: MoreLaw case result matches Nashville defendant; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Tyshawn Ford
profiles.description: Black Unity leader and Lane Community College student arrested at a peaceful Black Lives Matter march through Springfield, Oregon's Thurston Hills neighborhood on July 29, 2020, organized in response to a noose displayed near a Black family's home. Punched in the head by a Springfield officer and arrested, his criminal case was later dismissed and he became a plaintiff in CLDC's civil-rights suit against the police.
profiles.finding: Double Sided Media retrospective and independent assessment leads; Flickr image is by subject, not necessarily of him. Football/contractor namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Latroi Devon Newbins
profiles.description: Latroi Devon Newbins, 28, charged July 23, 2020 with arson in Salt Lake City after the May 30, 2020 BLM protest where he threw combustible material into a burning police car. Pleaded guilty; 13 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Deseret News explicitly captions 2019 booking portrait as LaTroi Devon Newbins and credits Salt Lake County Jail. Downloaded and visually inspected recognizable 800x1009 portrait; preserve watermark; rights not assumed public domain.

profiles.name: George Allen
profiles.description: George Allen, 31, of Pittsburgh, charged July 22, 2020 with civil disorder for damaging an occupied police vehicle by throwing an object through the front passenger window during the May 30, 2020 Pittsburgh BLM protest. Pleaded guilty; 12 months federal prison + 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Politician and coach namesakes excluded; Pittsburgh-specific follow-up remains.

profiles.name: Jeremy Trapp
profiles.description: On July 17, 2020 Jeremy Trapp, 24, was observed by an informant and NYPD officers attempting to cut the brake line of an NYPD van. He had been communicating with an undercover informant about wanting to cut brake lines on police vehicles, and participated in reconnaissance for a bridge he expressed wanting to set on fire — saying current protests weren't violent enough. He stated he wanted to harm police officers and supporters because they were racist and wanted to burn the bridge so that "white supremacists could not use it to get to Brooklyn from Staten Island." Sentenced to 18 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: CBS caption identifies subject and federal prosecutor credit; source image still pending quality inspection.

profiles.name: Cody Michael Tarner
profiles.description: Cody Michael Tarner, 23, of Hagerstown, MD, was indicted by a federal grand jury for burning two Supreme Court Police vehicles and attempting to burn a third on July 15, 2020. Tarner poured gasoline from a can into three Supreme Court Police vehicles, igniting two; he himself was engulfed in flames and suffered severe burns before a Supreme Court Police officer rendered first aid. One vehicle was destroyed, one damaged, the third did not catch fire. He was held without bond pending trial; tried unsuccessfully to plead insanity.
profiles.finding: Patch and federal court PDF leads; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Edward William Carubis
profiles.description: Edward William Carubis, 25, charged July 13, 2020 with assaulting federal officers in Portland by shining a green laser into three officers eyes. Pleaded guilty; 2 days time served.
profiles.finding: Federal affidavit and Street Roots case coverage; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Benjamin Wood-Pavich
profiles.description: Benjamin Wood-Pavich was federally charged with forcibly assaulting a federal officer during demonstrations outside the Mark O. Hatfield United States Courthouse in Portland on July 5, 2020. The government dismissed the case without prejudice on November 2, 2020. A later Justice Department comparison of Portland protest cases said it was unknown whether he had been arrested at the scene, and the available record does not establish booking or confinement.
profiles.finding: Street Roots and DOJ lists corroborate case; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Theodore Adriaan Matthee-O'Brien
profiles.description: Theodore Adriaan Matthee-O'Brien, 21, was charged with assaulting a federal officer on July 5, 2020 during ongoing Portland, OR protests after George Floyd's murder. He was arrested at a violent protest on July 6 — a student at the private liberal arts university Reed College. Found not guilty.
profiles.finding: Street Roots, Daily World and official charging-list leads; no accepted portrait.
